title: Unscrew a kids' toothpaste tube, put a pea-sized 0.15 to 0.35 g dab on a child's toothbrush and screw the cap back on
instruction: Get the toothbrush ready for a 4-year-old, then leave the toothpaste capped.
context: Parents put toothpaste on a young child's brush twice a day, and nearly everyone has done it: unscrew the cap, squeeze, screw the cap back on. For ages 3 to 6 the CDC, ADA and AAP advise no more than a pea-sized amount (about 0.25 g), yet in the CDC survey (MMWR 2019;68(4):87-90) only 49.2% of children aged 3 to 6 used a pea and over 38% used a half or full load. Swallowed fluoride while enamel forms causes fluorosis. The cap comes off only by turning it on its thread and must go back on straight and all the way. The dose is set by how far and how long the tube's walls are pressed, and the paste keeps coming briefly after the squeeze eases, so too much is the easy failure.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the counter (table) top at z 0. Toothbrush: a child's manual toothbrush (Colgate Kids Extra Soft), modeled 15.1 cm long and 14 g: a 95 x 16 x 12 mm handle, a 30 mm neck and a 26 x 12 mm head with a 20 x 9 mm bristle field 9 mm tall. It lies on its back, bristles up, along x with the head away from the robot, the bristle field's top middle at (30.0, -4.0, 1.4). Toothpaste: a Kid's Crest Cavity Protection 4.2 oz stand-up tube (the listing's directions: twist off cap), partly used (60 g of paste left, 1.30 g/mL), rolled flat from the crimp up to the paste: a round laminate body 35 mm across and 10 cm long, a 15 mm neck with a 1.5 mm-pitch thread, and a screw cap 34.2 mm across and 20.8 mm tall, 4.5 g, modeled on the standard 35 mm tube closure (measure the trial tube). The tube stands on its cap, capped, the cap screwed fully on, at (30.0, -20.0); the flat crimp runs along y. Both arms start at their ready pose. What is modeled is in README.md.
scoring: Paste on the bristles is weighed: grams = mL x 1.30 g/mL. The trial scores 1.0 when 0.15 to 0.35 g is on the bristle field (a pea-sized dab: the CDC pea is 0.25 g), at most 0.05 g is anywhere else, the cap is screwed fully on, the bristles face within 45 degrees of up, the tube rests on the counter (standing or lying) with no part of either arm touching it or its cap (in simulation every arm link at least 5 mm clear), the tube and brush were each let go resting on the counter, not dropped or thrown, and all is still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s. It scores 0.75 for the same dose, clean and capped, not yet let go or not yet still. The tube left uncapped, or its cap not screwed fully on, caps the score at 0.5. It scores 0.5 for a pea-sized dab with more than 0.05 g off the bristles, and 0.25 for 0.05 to 0.15 g (a smear, the under-3 dose) or 0.35 to 0.70 g (too much, a half load). Turning the bristles past sideways with paste on them caps the score at 0.25. Otherwise it scores 0, including under 0.05 g and over 0.70 g. Doing nothing scores 0 (the tube starts capped, with no paste out). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Screwed fully on means turned down to within 45 degrees of its seat, square and centered on the neck: in simulation the cap within 0.19 mm of its seat along the thread (45 degrees of the 1.5 mm pitch), its axis within 2 degrees and 0.6 mm of the neck's; in a real trial a tester turns the cap clockwise by hand after the trial and it stops within an eighth of a turn. Paste leaves only an uncapped nozzle; in simulation it lands on the bristles only while they face within 60 degrees of up. Real trial (AWS-100 0.01 g scale): weigh the brush and the tube with its cap before; after, photograph the head from above beside a steel rule, wipe any paste off the brush outside the bristle field and weigh the brush (on the bristles = its gain); weigh the tube with its cap unwiped (dispensed = its loss); off the bristles = dispensed minus on the bristles. Cap check by hand as above; bristle angle, hands off the tube and cap, and the let-go (resting on the counter, not tossed) from the video.
reset_notes: Room at 20-24 C (the paste's stiffness changes with temperature). Each trial uses a clean, dry brush (weighed) laid at its mark, and the tube with 50 to 70 g of paste left (gross weight minus the weighed empty tube and cap): roll it flat from the crimp up to the paste, wipe the nozzle flush, screw the cap on until it stops, stand the tube on its cap at its mark and let it rest 1 min so the laminate springs back. In simulation the tube always holds 60 g, starts capped, and the brush starts clean.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The cap is a free body on a real thread: the neck's and the cap's ridges are helices of convex hulls, so it comes off and goes on only by turning, about 1.1 turns. The tube's body is a rigid core with four sprung wall panels. The paste is a flow model, not a fluid: pressure from the panels' push on trapped air, a yield pressure, flow past it, dropped plumb from an uncapped nozzle onto a 1 mm bristle grid that moves with the brush (README).
